critical_code_review_comments: returns_routes.edit_sale correctly guards cancelled/returned invoices, re-computes subtotal/total with discount, enforces max_discount_percent and can_edit_prices, adjusts product stock using old/new quantity deltas (per product), and reconciles customer balance by first reverting old sale impact then applying new one. Audit entry via log_audit covers before/after client/total/remise/articles.

edit_sale uses sale['_id']=0 projection but response is returned directly (not response_model=Sale), fine. However if GET /api/sales/{id} is response_model=Sale, newly added fields (edited_at/edited_by/edit_count/returns_total) must be in Sale model - verified present in server.py (~line 167-181).

create_return performs stock +qty (customer) or -qty (supplier) BEFORE issuing the return number via next_sequence; if next_sequence or any downstream step fails, stock change wouldn't rollback. Low-risk here (no transactions) but worth noting as atomicity caveat.
create_return applies applied_on_source to source.balance_due and sets sale.status='returned'; combined with edit_sale's refusal to edit returned invoices, this correctly prevents double-counting.
Audit list endpoint is /api/audit-logs (not /api/audit) - documentation note for future testers.
server.py is still >1700 lines; consider extracting sales/returns/orders routers (tracked carry-over from iter6/7).
